newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's 1996 grain imports doubled on 1995 levels.
newsitem.headline: Russia's 1996 grain imports doubled on 1995 levels.

text.p: Russia's grain and flour imports of 5.1 million tonnes in 1996 were more than double 1995's 2.3 million tonnes, a rise of 116 percent year-on-year, State Customs Committee figures showed on Tuesday.
The data, carried by Interfax news agency, put the value of last year's total grain imports including flour at $913.2 million against $192.2 million in 1995.
It said wheat and wheat-rye blend imports in 1996 of 2.7 million tonnes were over 15 times 1995 levels. No comparison figures were provided.

Wheat-flour imports of 687,400 tonnes represented a sevenfold increase on the previous year, while rye imports of 264,500 tonnes fell 25 percent. Barley imports of 1.4 million slipped 20 percent year-on-year.
Exports of Russian grain and flour in 1996 slumped to 642,800 tonnes, down 77 percent from the 2.7 million tonnes delivered abroad in 1995.
Earnings from grain exports last year were $135.1 million, against $395.4 million in 1995.

Wheat and wheat-rye blend exports of 343,000 tonnes in 1996 were a mere 22 percent of 1995 levels. Rye exports of 8,800 tonnes fell 80 percent year-on-year, barley exports of 187,900 tonnes fell 70 percent and wheat flour exports of 103,000 tonnes plummeted by 81 percent.
State Customs Committee figures do not include unregistered transactions.
